title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
authors: Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li, Siyao Xiao, Runqing Cheng, Xiao Lin, Zhifang Liu, Haoqian Wang

tldr.zh: DexCast 从人类 RGB-D 视频重建并修正手物交互，生成机器人示范，以训练与真机一致形式的手—物体点云作为几何观测，结合预训练的骨架时序运动编码驱动扩散策略，实现无需真机遥操作示范的操作学习与动作块间闭环执行。
tldr.en: DexCast reconstructs and refines hand–object interactions from human RGB-D videos to generate robot demonstrations, uses hand/object point clouds in a common training/deployment format as geometric observations, and conditions a diffusion policy on pretrained skeletal-temporal motion features, enabling learning without robot teleoperation demonstrations and closed-loop execution between action chunks.

evaluation_scope.zh: 沿用手物重建与残差 RL 修正生成示范并做空间扩增；训练和部署均从网格采样手／物体完整点云，真机由关节状态与正运动学生成手点云、由 FoundationPose 估计物体位姿更新物体点云。DMPM 在超过 500 万帧重定向运动上预训练 VAE，冻结编码器将最近 32 帧关节位置／速度变成 256 维历史特征，与 SIM(3) 等变几何特征及本体状态共同条件化扩散网络；潜在码是观测条件，不是待预测的跨手动作码。UR5＋12 自由度 XHAND 验证抓取、倾倒、翻正、按压、擦拭、堆叠六任务，每任务从一段人类视频生成 40 条示范并分别训练策略。两视角平均成功率为 87.5%／86.7%；预测的 32 步指令以 8 Hz 全部执行后重新感知，只执行位置目标。当前限刚体物体；换手需重新设计骨架并训练 DMPM。
evaluation_scope.en: Existing HOI reconstruction and residual-RL refinement generate spatially augmented demonstrations. Training/deployment sample complete hand/object mesh point clouds; hardware updates hand geometry from joints/FK and object geometry from FoundationPose tracking. A VAE-based DMPM pretrained on >5M retargeted frames is frozen to encode 32 joint-position/velocity frames into a 256-D history feature, conditioning diffusion alongside SIM(3)-equivariant geometry and proprioception. This latent conditions observations rather than serving as a predicted cross-hand action code. UR5 + 12-DoF XHAND tests grasping, pouring, flipping, pressing, wiping and stacking, with 40 generated demonstrations from one human video per task and separately trained policies. Viewpoint averages are 87.5%/86.7%. All 32 predicted commands execute at 8 Hz before replanning; only position targets are applied. Rigid objects only; new hands require new skeleton design and DMPM training.
